name: WAYSTAR HOLDING

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The counter to my refusal is that I am hiding behind the discount rate on a name where the cheap case is specific. Correct the missing interest add-back and the market requires only +4.7% five-year growth from a business growing revenue 21% with subscription revenue up 34% and a 43% adjusted EBITDA margin - and it is simultaneously in a live sale process run by Evercore. That is a free option on a control premium sitting on top of a business the market is asking almost nothing of. Arguing it away with a beta I invented, when the engine's own regression says 0.71, is exactly the kind of move that makes a model unfalsifiable.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Fourth-quarter and full-year unlevered free cash flow against the $269.0M nine-month figure and the $285.3M prior-year comparison - the single number that decides whether the income-statement growth is real. And whether the strategic process produces an agreement or is abandoned.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The decisive fact is already visible and it is why the counter loses. Nine-month unlevered free cash flow of $269.0M against $285.3M is DOWN 5.7%, and nine-month operating cash flow of $248.2M against $243.0M is up only 2.1%, in a period when revenue grew 21% and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 43%. That is the HURN, AGYS and TMDX cash-conversion break, no flag names it, and it means the base I would be correcting upward is not actually growing. Add the mechanism: capitalised software development more than doubled to $27.9M, which raises adjusted EBITDA and lowers free cash flow by construction. So the cheap case rests on a base the company's own cash statement says is flat. On the sale process I have no edge at all - an unsigned exploration reported by Reuters in September, with nothing since, is not a thesis.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I could not settle the discount rate, and it sets the sign. Beta is 0.71 at R-squared 0.085 - below the 0.15 threshold this file treats as the failed-beta condition - giving a 7.8% WACC at a 22% debt weight for a company that is 99% goodwill by book and still carries $1.46bn of LBO debt; at a defensible 1.0-1.2 beta the WACC is 9.0-9.9%, and the corrected-base requirement moves from +4.7% to +12.3%. The schema has no cost-of-equity field, so on this name the verdict is the output and no fair value is honest. I also could not learn anything about the sale process beyond the September report, and the news store carries nothing on this name after 2026-09-16.

what_changed: Q3 2026 (2026-11-02): revenue $325.6M, up 21%; adjusted EBITDA $139.3M at a 43% margin; subscription revenue $180.7M up 34%, volume-based $142.9M up 8%, provider $243.4M up 28%, patient $82.2M up 5%; cash flow from operations $103.9M and unlevered free cash flow $114.8M. Full-year 2026 guidance: revenue $1.277-1.287bn, adjusted EBITDA $543-549M, non-GAAP net income $322-337M, non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.63-1.71. But the nine-month cash figures run the other way and are the most important thing in the filing: operating cash flow of $248.2M against $243.0M a year earlier, up just 2.1%, and UNLEVERED FREE CASH FLOW of $269.0M against $285.3M - DOWN 5.7% - on revenue up 21% and an expanding adjusted EBITDA margin. The company's own MD&A attributes the investing swing partly to 'more purchases of property and equipment and an increase of capitalized software development costs', and capitalised software development more than doubled from $13.5M in nine-month 2025 to $27.9M in nine-month 2026. Separately, on 2026-09-15 Reuters reported Evercore had been hired to explore strategic options including a potential sale; the stock rose on the report and no agreement has been announced.
consensus_case: Waystar is a healthcare payments platform compounding revenue 21% with a 43% adjusted EBITDA margin, and at $27.70 the market is paying $6.52bn of enterprise value - about 12x guided 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $543-549M and 5.1x guided revenue of $1.28bn. The case for that price is the quality of the growth mix: third-quarter subscription revenue up 34% to $180.7M while volume-based revenue grew 8%, and provider revenue up 28%. The case the price also reflects is harder: the equity sits on $4.01bn of goodwill against $4.04bn of book from the EQT and Bain leveraged buyout, with $1.46bn of debt still outstanding, and the stock is down 24% over twelve months. And since 2026-09-15 the name has carried deal optionality rather than only business value - Reuters reported Waystar had hired Evercore to explore strategic options including a sale, which is what the 63-day return of +9.7% against a falling twelve-month line is pricing.
base_case_rationale: No number is recordable because the discount rate decides the sign and the schema cannot reach it, but the central case is roughly +7% five-year FCFF growth against a market requirement that runs +4.7% to +23.8% depending on inputs I cannot settle. The base needs raising: interest_expense is recorded as None against $1,463.7M of debt, so the FCFF base of $212.8M carries no after-tax add-back at all, and the 10-Q reports net interest expense of $18,182k in the quarter and $56,531k over nine months - roughly $75M a year, worth about $56M after tax. On the two-year mean that takes the base to about $269M, and on the newest year plus the add-back to about $339M; the company's own unlevered free cash flow, which is nearly the same construction, runs about $349M for 2026. But the reason I sit at +7% rather than higher is the conversion break: unlevered free cash flow DOWN 5.7% over nine months while revenue grew 21% says the thing a DCF discounts is not currently growing at all, and part of the 43% adjusted EBITDA margin is manufactured by capitalising development cost that used to be expensed - $27.9M over nine months against $13.5M, a transfer from the cash flow statement to adjusted EBITDA.
key_risks: Nine-month unlevered free cash flow DOWN 5.7% and operating cash flow up only 2.1% while revenue grew 21% - the income statement and the cash statement disagree
Capitalised software development more than doubled to $27.9M over nine months, which raises adjusted EBITDA and reduces free cash flow by construction
Beta 0.71 at R-squared 0.085 gives a 7.8% WACC on a company 99% goodwill by book with $1.46bn of LBO debt; at a defensible beta the required growth doubles and the schema cannot override it
Goodwill of $4.01bn against book equity of $4.04bn - tangible book is deeply negative
A strategic process reported in September with no agreement since; if it concludes without a deal the premium in the 63-day return unwinds
watch_for: Q4 and full-year 2026 unlevered free cash flow against the $269.0M nine-month figure and $285.3M prior-year comparison
Capitalised software development in Q4 - whether the step-up from $13.5M to $27.9M continues
Any announced transaction, or confirmation that the Evercore process has ended
Volume-based revenue growth, currently 8% against subscription at 34% - the mix shift is the quality of the business
